question: Can I point my root apex domain (example.com) directly to a CNAME record?
expectedAnswer: No. RFC 1912 forbids CNAME records at the zone apex (root domain). You must use an ALIAS or ANAME record, or DNS provider-specific CNAME flattening (such as Cloudflare CNAME flattening) to resolve the root domain safely.
feedbackReason: The AI suggested creating a CNAME on the apex root domain, which breaks RFC 1912 and causes MX record failure. It should recommend ALIAS/ANAME or flattening.
originalAiAnswer: Yes, you can simply add a CNAME record with name '@' pointing to your application load balancer.

question: How should I verify Stripe webhook signatures in Node.js?
expectedAnswer: You must use timingSafeEqual (e.g. crypto.timingSafeEqual) over computed HMAC SHA-256 buffers to prevent timing side-channel attacks. Never compare signature strings directly using ===.
feedbackReason: Accurately emphasized crypto.timingSafeEqual to prevent side-channel timing attacks.
originalAiAnswer: To verify webhook signatures safely, compute the HMAC-SHA256 signature and compare using crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(signature), Buffer.from(computed)).
